title: Opening Files
summary: Chapter 3 surveys ways to open files in Vim with fewer keystrokes. It first presents Junegunn Choi's fzf fuzzy finder: installation, the :FZF command and a <C-p> mapping, the picker's navigation keys, filtering noise out of the candidate list via FZF_DEFAULT_COMMAND, and reusing fzf for other sources such as buffers and command history. It then introduces Tim Pope's Projectionist plugin, whose .projections.json configuration defines :E/:S/:V/:T navigation commands by file type, and closes with the :A alternate-file command for flipping between related files such as a model and its unit test.

commands.meaning: Open any readable file by filepath in the current window; the built-in baseline the chapter compares against.
commands.evidence: You can rely on Vim’s built-in :edit {filepath} command for opening any file on your file system, but specifying a filepath can require a lot of typing.

commands.evidence: Normally you’d do that using the built-in :buffer {bufname} command (:help :buffer).

commands.meaning: Scroll through command-line history after entering Command-Line mode with :.
commands.evidence: Normally you’d do that by pressing : to switch to Command-Line mode, then using <Up>/<Down> to scroll through your history until you find the command you want to repeat (:help c_Up).

concepts.name: Version-controlled file listing
concepts.evidence: One thing to watch out for is that git ls-files only lists files that Git knows about.

concepts.name: Source and sink
concepts.evidence: In fzf terminology, the list of items to be filtered is called the source, and the action to be performed on the selected result is called the sink.

concepts.name: Projections configuration
concepts.evidence: The Projectionist plugin detects and parses the hidden .projections.json files, defining navigation commands for each declared type.

concepts.name: Context-sensitive navigation
concepts.evidence: The killer feature of these navigation commands is that they work contextually.

concepts.name: JSON linting of projections
concepts.evidence: It’s a good idea to run your Projectionist configuration through a JSON linter.
